npc:agathelos-the-raging.text: Agathelos the Raging. Agathelos the Raging is a colossal armored boar penned within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. To the quilboar, whose god and progenitor is the great boar Agamaggan, a beast of his size carries considerable spiritual significance, and he grows even more fearsome when enraged. His sheer mass and strength make him one of the most dangerous beasts lurking under the southern Barrens. The god and progenitor of the quilboar is Agamaggan, a titanic boar. A beast the size of Agathelos—standing roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard—therefore carries considerable spiritual significance among the Razorfen tribes. The quilboar do not let Agathelos roam loose within the Kraul. He is kept in a short, dead-end tunnel behind a field maintained by several quilboar guards. Should intruders break past the barrier, they face a raging beast that grows even bigger and more terrifying when enraged.

npc:aggem-thorncurse.text: Aggem Thorncurse. Aggem Thorncurse is a living quilboar shaman in Razorfen Kraul, bearing the title Death's Head Prophet. He calls a boar spirit to his aid when threatened. Aggem guards a part of Razorfen Kraul occupied by the Death's Head tribe. His shamanic powers include summoning a boar spirit, reflecting the quilboar's reverence for Agamaggan.

npc:aku-mai.text: Aku'mai. Aku'mai is a monstrous, three-headed hydra dwelling in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps along the Zoram Strand. A servant of an Old God, it rose from the waters when that Old God's corruption tainted the temple's sacred Moon Well. The Twilight's Hammer cult has gathered in the Deeps and sacrifices innocents to it for power. Blackfathom Deeps was once a great temple of Elune, until the corruption of an Old God seeped up from beneath the earth and tainted its sacred Moon Well. Aku'mai, a gargantuan hydra and servant of the Old God, rose from the waters. Rather than an ordinary denizen of the tides, Aku'mai is a living blight upon the Zoram Strand that has taken up residence in the submerged ruins of the night elves' fallen temple, poisoning the waters with its malice.

npc:arcanist-doan.text: Arcanist Doan. Arcanist Doan is a master human mage residing within the Athenaeum of the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing. He serves the Scarlet Crusade as one of its most lethal arcane specialists and guardian of key crusade archives. While the fanatical ranks of the Scarlet Crusade lean heavily on martial fury and holy fervor, Doan remained convinced that raw arcane power was essential to purging the Scourge from Lordaeron. Stationed deep inside the Athenaeum of the Monastery's library, he was entrusted as both a lorekeeper and an operational gatekeeper, safeguarding the Scarlet Key that secures crusade sanctuaries across the northern kingdoms.

npc:baron-aquanis.text: Baron Aquanis. Baron Aquanis is a powerful water elemental of the flooded Moonshrine Ruins in Blackfathom Deeps, where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair. He rises from the deep water when someone disturbs the ruins' Fathom Stone. The shamans of the Earthen Ring have long thought him a corrupted elemental power, and they suspect the cult is behind it. Submerged beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Stone lies right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who now occupy the ruins. Inside it is a fathom core, a device that, properly read, tells the history of all elemental activity around it. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover the core, and disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

npc:baron-silverlaine.text: Baron Silverlaine. Baron Silverlaine was the rightful human lord of the fortress once known as Silverlaine Keep, perched high above Pyrewood Village. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the savage worgen upon the region, the baron was mercilessly slaughtered. Now, his tormented spirit lingers in the ruined dining hall, bound in undeath to defend the very lair that became his tomb. Before the shadow of the wolf-beasts blanketed the southern hills of Silverpine, Baron Silverlaine ruled over a proud noble estate. His fortress provided safety and oversight to the surrounding lands. That peace shattered when Archmage Arugal, seeking a weapon against the rampaging Scourge, unleashed summoned worgen into the region. The feral monstrosities could not be controlled; they stormed the stronghold, overran its guards, and butchered the baron. Death brought no release to Baron Silverlaine. Bound to the keep's ancient Great Hall, his restless ghost now wanders the trashed dining tables where he once feasted. The cursed lord lashes out at intruders who enter his ruined home.

npc:bazil-thredd.text: Bazil Thredd. Bazil Thredd is Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant and most trusted assistant, locked in the Stormwind Stockade since the Stonemasons' riots. Now the prison has risen in revolt, and Thredd leads the rioting Defias inmates from its eastern cell block. When the Stonemasons Guild was refused payment by the nobility of Stormwind for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef rejected government appeasements and sparked open revolt. Bazil Thredd stood at VanCleef's side as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. During the violent clashes that followed, Thredd was captured by the city guard. While VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood, Thredd was cast into the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. For years, Thredd remained silent and seemingly forsaken behind iron bars. That isolation shattered with a massive prison riot that overran the guards, opening the cells and turning the Stockade into an armed fortress right under the Mage Quarter. Taking leadership of the imprisoned Defias bandits, insurgents, and allied cutthroats, Thredd established his command post in the eastern wing under the guard of an ogre named Hamhock. Warden Thelwater, desperate to restore order before the chaos spills into the city streets, demands Thredd's head to break the rebellion's leadership.

npc:bazzalan.text: Bazzalan. Bazzalan commands the Searing Blade cult from the lava caverns beneath Orgrimmar. Alongside Jergosh the Invoker, he directs its work in Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Bazzalan has joined the Searing Blade cult in Ragefire Chasm. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, the satyr rogue commands the cult's field forces from winding lava caverns. He is swift and lethal with twin blades. From a volcanic ledge above the central chamber, Bazzalan oversees the cultist guards. Jergosh the Invoker conducts demonic rituals below. Like all satyrs, Bazzalan's ultimate loyalty belongs to demonic masters. He uses poison, quick strikes, and stealth against Horde scouts who venture near the cult's staging ground.

npc:blind-hunter.text: Blind Hunter. The Blind Hunter is an elusive, albino bat that roosts deep within Razorfen Kraul. Unlike the ordinary bats nesting near the cavern entrances, this rare creature prowls the sunless depths of the quilboar redoubt. Razorfen Kraul is riddled with winding briars and dark subterranean caverns. While common Kraul bats roost nearer to the surface where faint light filters in from the outside world, the Blind Hunter has adapted entirely to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale, albino hide and milky gaze are likely the result of generations spent completely isolated from natural sunlight. True to its name, scholars and scouts believe the creature has lost most or all of its conventional eyesight, relying instead on keen senses of hearing and echolocation to track prey through the gloom. It rarely shows itself, appearing only on occasion to hunt through the dense thickets, making an encounter with this phantom beast a prized occurrence among cavern explorers.

npc:bloodmage-thalnos.text: Bloodmage Thalnos. Bloodmage Thalnos is a skeletal spellcaster who haunts the Graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Who he was in life is not recorded, but the plague of undeath claimed him, and he now lingers deep within the Crusade's holy grounds, hungering for vengeance. No record tells who Thalnos was in life. Whatever his past, the plague of undeath claimed him. Rather than being cleansed or permanently destroyed, he rose as a withered skeleton, still clinging to his fiery magic and arcane mastery, and crying out for vengeance and for more souls. Confined to the deepest corner of the monastery's courtyard tombs, Thalnos commands apparitions and shambling undead minions against anyone who disturbs his domain. His continued presence poses a bitter contradiction for the Crusade: an undead monstrosity lingering right beneath their sacred halls, embodying the very horror they swore an eternity to eradicate.

npc:bruegal-ironknuckle.text: Bruegal Ironknuckle. Bruegal Ironknuckle is an infamous dwarven prisoner held within the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the petty criminals and rioting rabble that fill the holding cells, he is a formidable brawler whose presence deep inside the corridors spells immediate danger to anyone trying to restore order. When the Stormwind Stockade erupted into open revolt, many of the city's most volatile cutthroats took control of the subterranean cellblocks. Among them is Bruegal Ironknuckle, a particularly dangerous dwarf inmate known for brutal brawling strength. Rather than staying confined to a single cell, he prowls the riot-torn hallways, ready to bash anyone attempting to quell the uprising. While much of the uprising inside the facility is orchestrated by the Defias Brotherhood and their ringleaders, inmates like Bruegal highlight that the prison houses assorted rogues and outlaws from across the eastern realms. Whatever crimes earned him a sentence deep beneath Stormwind, his fierce resilience makes him an elusive target and one of the deadliest lone inmates walking the prison corridors.

npc:captain-greenskin.text: Captain Greenskin. Captain Greenskin is an elite goblin pirate overseeing the construction and crew of Edwin VanCleef's massive ironclad juggernaut. Hidden deep in the subterranean cove of the Deadmines, he commands the pirate forces hired by the Defias Brotherhood. His goal is to bring the warship to readiness to sail against Stormwind. Pacing the main deck of the gigantic juggernaut under construction in the Deadmines cove, Captain Greenskin represents the naval backbone of the Defias conspiracy. A seasoned goblin mariner, Greenskin was brought into Edwin VanCleef's inner circle to turn an underground cavern into a drydock for an engine of war. Greenskin does not command an ordinary crew of stonemasons or bandits. Under his direct watch serve seasoned cutthroats, including his fearsome tauren first mate Mr. Smite and the murloc ship's cook, Cookie. Together, they hold the ship's gangplanks and upper deck, standing between intruders and VanCleef's private cabin atop the bridge.

npc:charlga-razorflank.text: Charlga Razorflank. Charlga Razorflank, widely known as the Crone of the Kraul, is the fierce and cunning geomancer chieftain presiding over Razorfen Kraul. Under her leadership, the Razorfen quilboar drove the tauren out of the southern Barrens through ruthless expansion. Within the tangled, massive brambles of Razorfen Kraul rules Charlga Razorflank. Revered by her people as a master geomancer whose experimental magic remains unmatched among quilboar, Charlga organized her fractious kin into a unified, lethal threat. She harnessed the primal earth and giant thorns sprouting from the demigod Agamaggan's remains, reshaping the labyrinthine Kraul into an impenetrable fortress.

npc:commander-springvale.text: Commander Springvale. Commander Springvale was once a devoted paladin and a commander at Shadowfang Keep. Slain alongside his men during the feral worgen slaughter orchestrated by Archmage Arugal, his vengeful spirit remains behind to haunt the castle halls. Even in death, his ghost fiercely guards the keep against all who enter. Before the ruin of Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale stood as an honorable paladin dedicated to the Holy Light. Leading the garrison in Silverpine Forest, he oversaw the keep's security during the fraught days following the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge. When Archmage Arugal summoned the extraplanar worgen to bolster Dalaran's failing ranks against the undead Scourge, the wild beasts quickly slipped from the mage's control. The ravenous pack descended upon the fortress, slaughtering Baron Silverlaine and his entire guard. Springvale perished in the halls he had sworn to protect, his service violently cut short. Death offered no release to Springvale. His ghost haunts the keep's council room alongside its spectral soldiers. He still wields paladin powers, including Holy Light and Hammer of Justice, against intruders.

npc:cookie.text: Cookie. Cookie is an elite murloc serving as the ship's cook aboard the juggernaut hidden deep within the Deadmines. An unusual recruit among the Defias Brotherhood, he tends the crew's cauldrons beneath the watchful eye of Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. He is the only entirely optional boss encountered within the underground dry dock. Beneath the decks of the towering juggernaut in the Ironclad Cove, cooking duty falls neither to a human outrider nor a goblin engineer, but to a solitary murloc known simply as Cookie. How he came by the position is anyone's guess. Whatever doubts the rest of the crew might harbor about a murloc presiding over their rations, pirates are rarely in a position to be picky, and in the underworld of Moonbrook, a meal is a meal. Cookie patrols the waterways and shores around the pirate flagship, wielding his cooking utensils alongside acidic brews. Despite being isolated from typical murloc tribes, he defends his cauldron with savage ferocity, flinging caustic concoctions at any intruders who wander into the docks. Because his station sits away from the main gangplanks, many who storm the cove bypass his kitchen entirely, making him the only optional overseer aboard the Defias juggernaut.

npc:dark-iron-ambassador.text: Dark Iron Ambassador. The Dark Iron Ambassador is an emissary of the Dark Iron clan found deep within Gnomeregan. His presence raises questions about the clan's interest in the ruined gnome capital. The Dark Iron Ambassador is found among the dangers of irradiated Gnomeregan. He represents the Dark Iron clan, but the purpose of his mission is not explained.

npc:dextren-ward.text: Dextren Ward. Dextren Ward is an infamous criminal and grave robber locked away inside the Stormwind Stockade. Before his capture, he profited by exhuming bodies from Duskwood's Raven Hill Cemetery and delivering them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Now caught in the midst of the prison's bloody uprising, he remains marked for death by the town council of Darkshire. Before ending up in chains beneath the streets of Stormwind, Dextren Ward conducted a grim and lucrative business in the fog-choked woods of Duskwood. Raven Hill Cemetery was already a site of sorrow and growing horror, but Ward treated its burial grounds as a private quarry. Rather than hunting merely for trinkets and heirlooms left with the dead, Ward dealt in flesh, unearthing fresh graves to supply local dark practitioners. Ward's primary customer was Morbent Fel, a necromancer whose dark rituals have plagued Duskwood and swelled the ranks of the undead. In supplying bodies to Fel, Ward actively contributed to the terror that grips Darkshire. Though eventually caught by Stormwind authorities and dragged into the Stockade, his crimes earned him the undying enmity of the people of Duskwood, prompting Councilman Millstipe to demand Ward's hand as proof of justice served. When a sweeping rebellion broke out inside the Stockade, Ward was not liberated by allies, but rather freed from his cell to join the chaos within the locked-down dungeon. Armed and vicious, he commands his own corner of the prison and uses terror to ward off interlopers, making him one of the priority targets Alliance forces seek to eliminate while restoring order.

npc:edwin-vancleef.text: Edwin VanCleef. Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant Guildmaster of the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. After being cheated of payment by the House of Nobles, he led a violent workers' revolt and formed the outlaw Defias Brotherhood. Operating from deep within the Deadmines of Westfall, he seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore. Following the devastation of the First War, Edwin VanCleef was chosen to lead the Stonemasons Guild in the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City. A peerless craftsman and an idealist, VanCleef directed the construction of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals. Alongside his mastery of architecture, VanCleef was a remarkably deadly operative; he was trained in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft by his childhood friend, Mathias Shaw. When the years of labor concluded, the House of Nobles ran up colossal debts through military campaigns and refused to provide the Stonemasons their promised compensation. Enraged, VanCleef demanded restitution, only for the nobles to officially dissolve the guild. Leading a riot, VanCleef took the Stonemasons out of the city; in the chaos his lieutenant and most trusted assistant, Bazil Thredd, was captured and left to languish in the Stockade. In Westfall, VanCleef gathered his exiled workers and allied outcasts beneath the banner of the Defias Brotherhood.

npc:electrocutioner-6000.text: Electrocutioner 6000. The Electrocutioner 6000 is a deadly, super-charged spider tank deployed to defend the Launch Bay within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan. It fights for Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the leper gnomes who follow him, holding the upper platform against anyone pushing deeper into the fallen city. Gnomeregan's fall left its war machines in the hands of Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the irradiated leper gnomes who still follow him. The Electrocutioner 6000, a hulking spider tank crackling with high-voltage current, stands guard on the upper platform of Gnomeregan's Launch Bay and lashes intruders with electricity. The machine also guards a prize: the Workshop Key, which opens Gnomeregan's back door into its workshops. Those who bring down the Electrocutioner can claim the key and a quicker route into the city's depths.

npc:fenrus-the-devourer.text: Fenrus the Devourer. Fenrus the Devourer is an enormous worg that prowls the upper sanctum of Shadowfang Keep. Kept as a personal pet and guardian by Archmage Arugal, the ravenous beast is bloated on unnatural magics. Anyone daring to breach the archmage's personal study must contend with this feral horror and the master who watches over it. Deep within Shadowfang Keep, just outside Archmage Arugal's personal chambers, lurks the monstrous worg known as Fenrus the Devourer. Unlike the lupine worgen roaming the ramparts, Fenrus is an actual worg, swollen to gargantuan proportions. Prowling the shelves, scrolls, and arcane apparatuses of Arugal's private study, the beast serves both as a pet and as a violent perimeter guard against any intruder seeking the mad mage's head. Fenrus's unnatural bulk suggests he was subjected to the dark magics saturating the keep since Baron Silverlaine's downfall. Archmage Arugal or his unleashed worgen clearly warped the creature with arcane or shadowy experiments, transforming a native predator into a ravenous juggernaut. Fenrus is so feral and magically bound that no hunter can charm or tame his mind.

npc:gelihast.text: Gelihast. Gelihast is a ferocious, twin-blade wielding murloc chieftain residing in the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps. Surrounded by his Blindlight murlocs, he guards a strange altar in the flooded ruins of the sunken temple. While most murlocs stay near coastal shallows, Gelihast has claimed a lair deep in the sunken temple of Blackfathom Deeps beneath the Zoram Strand. Wielding twin swords with blinding speed, he cuts down intruders before they can react, and casters who stray into his reach rarely survive. Gelihast rules the Pool of Ask'ar, surrounded by his Blindlight brood, who swarm to his side at the first sign of trouble. Beyond his lair stands an altar; those who defeat him and touch it receive the Blessing of Blackfathom.

npc:ghamoo-ra-classic.text: Ghamoo-ra. Ghamoo-ra is an ancient, giant sea turtle inhabiting the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps, the sunken temple of Elune now overrun by the Twilight's Hammer cult. Armored in a massive shell, he savagely tramples any intruders who approach his island. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple dedicated to Elune, now flooded and claimed by naga, satyr and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among its drowned ruins, an enormous turtle whose thick shell turns aside all but the most determined blows. Ghamoo-ra roams a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar, surrounded by lesser turtles that leave travelers be. He alone attacks, crushing any who come near beneath his trampling bulk.

npc:gilnid.text: Gilnid. Gilnid, known as the Smelter, is the goblin master engineer running the forges in the depths of the Deadmines. He oversees the smelting of raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. Without his fiery operations, the Defias Brotherhood would lack the heavy cannons needed to assault Stormwind. Deep within the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood relies on industrial expertise to forge weapons of war. Gilnid serves as VanCleef's head smelter, commanding a small army of goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths in the central foundry. Towering over most of his kin, he drives his crew relentlessly through smoke and slag, barking orders and refusing breaks to ensure raw iron ore is processed into heavy plating and lethal ordnance.

npc:hamhock.text: Hamhock. Hamhock is a massive two-headed ogre confined within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Locked away beneath the capital alongside hardened Defias insurgents and cutthroats, he looms as a particularly brutal and unexpected inmate amidst the prison riot. The Stormwind Stockade was built to hold petty thieves, murderers, and political dissidents, making a towering two-headed ogre an imposing sight among the cells. When the prisoners rose up and took control of the facility, Hamhock remained entrenched in the chaos, crushing anyone foolish enough to intrude on his cellblock. No record explains how Hamhock was captured or why a two-headed ogre was locked away among Stormwind's thieves and dissidents. Whatever brought him to the Stockade, he is now one of its most dangerous inmates.

npc:herod.text: Herod. Herod is a renowned champion and berserker of the Scarlet Crusade, commanding the Armory within the Scarlet Monastery. Known for his ferocious martial prowess and unyielding zeal, he trains recruits in the brutal melee combat needed to wage holy war. His death is sought by both Alliance dissidents and the Horde's rulers in Undercity to weaken the Crusade's military core. Within the fortified halls of the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, Herod stands as the embodiment of the Crusade's martial aggression. Unlike the spellcasters and paladins who channel holy magic in the Cathedral, Herod relies on raw, bloodthirsty physical power. Clad in mail and wielding a massive two-handed axe, he personally trains cohorts of Scarlet Trainees, instilling a furious devotion to exterminating anyone not allied with their fanatical cause. Because Herod oversees the armaments and martial training of the Crusade's front-line warriors, taking him down is essential for anyone seeking to dismantle the order. Raleigh the Devout, an ex-Crusader disillusioned with the order's madness residing in Southshore, calls for Herod's demise to shatter their military leadership. Across Lordaeron, the dreadlord Varimathras in the Undercity similarly seeks his execution to clear out a dangerous human bastion bordering Forsaken territory.

npc:high-inquisitor-fairbanks.text: High Inquisitor Fairbanks. High Inquisitor Fairbanks was once a revered priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Betrayed, executed, and hidden away behind a secret door in the Scarlet Monastery Cathedral, his rotting, undead form stands as a grim monument to the Scarlet Crusade's dark descent. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Fairbanks was a respected holy man among the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor of Highlord Alexandros Mograine, the bearer of the legendary Ashbringer. He stood beside the Highlord when Mograine, High General Abbendis and Grand Inquisitor Isillien founded the Scarlet Crusade, at first a noble order sworn to destroy the Scourge.

npc:houndmaster-loksey.text: Houndmaster Loksey. Houndmaster Loksey is the officer charged with breeding and training the fearsome war dogs of the Scarlet Crusade. Stationed in the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing, he directs packs of hounds to hunt down undead, intruders, and perceived heretics. His merciless discipline has made the Monastery's beasts infamous throughout Tirisfal Glades. Within the heavily fortified walls of the Scarlet Monastery, Houndmaster Loksey commands the training of vicious tracking and attack dogs. The Scarlet Crusade relies on these trained hounds to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down any survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey holds absolute authority over the hounds guarding the Library wing, ensuring his charges are primed to tear intruders apart limb by limb. Loksey is not the only beast handler in his family serving the cause. His brother, Huntsman Leopold, serves as the Scarlet Crusade's envoy to the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope Chapel. Leopold holds a low opinion of his brother, privately asserting that Loksey can barely manage his own hounds, let alone represent the order in high-stakes diplomacy. Despite Leopold's scorn, Loksey remains a key officer within the Monastery's inner hierarchy.

npc:interrogator-vishas.text: Interrogator Vishas. Interrogator James Vishas is the Scarlet Crusade's master of torment, stationed deep within the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing. Infamous for his shrill voice and sheer cruelty, he takes twisted pleasure in breaking captives and testing the limits of mortal flesh. Few who enter his torture chambers ever leave with their minds or bodies intact. Within the dark crypts and burial grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas tends to the Crusade's captive enemies. While the zealots outside march in gleaming armor under banners of purity, Vishas represents the grim reality behind their crusade: unbridled sadism cloaked in religious righteous fury. He approaches interrogation not merely as an intelligence duty, but as a prized craft, reveling in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and any living travelers unlucky enough to be branded heretics.

npc:jergosh-the-invoker.text: Jergosh the Invoker. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Jergosh the Invoker plots against the Horde. He leads Searing Blade cultists in Ragefire Chasm and practices demonic arts while Thrall guides the orcs toward honor and shamanism. Jergosh gathers the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. While Thrall leads the orcs toward honor and shamanism, Jergosh turns to demonic power. He hides in Ragefire Chasm, where he draws followers into a sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. From below the Horde capital, the cult works against the path the new Horde has chosen.

npc:kam-deepfury.text: Kam Deepfury. Kam Deepfury is a notorious Dark Iron saboteur incarcerated within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the majority of the prison's inmates, he has no allegiance to the Defias Brotherhood, having been captured for orchestrating a devastating explosion along the Thandol Span far to the north. While the Stockade is overwhelmingly filled with disgruntled Stonemasons and Defias rebels, Kam Deepfury stands apart. A Dark Iron dwarf of cunning and violence, Deepfury was captured and brought to Stormwind after masterminding an operation that crippled vital northern infrastructure. He is locked deep within the prison's cells, isolated from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain but just as hostile to the Alliance as any rebel rioter sharing the corridors. Alliance intelligence stationed at Dun Modr, near the northern border of the Wetlands, identified Deepfury as the chief architect behind the explosion that shattered the Thandol Span. The blast severed one of the massive stone bridges linking the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands. Beyond crippling a critical trade and military route for Ironforge and the Alliance, the sabotage claimed the life of a kin of the dwarf commander Longbraid the Grim.

npc:lady-anacondra.text: Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once one of the night elf druids who followed Naralex in his ambitious effort to heal the Barrens, she was lost when her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare. Her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a drive to remake the land to match that twisted dream. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was one of Naralex's druids. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she followed him into the caverns. Her loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering her sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession. Now styling herself Lady Anacondra, she stands guard among the first subterranean chambers of the Wailing Caverns. Like her fellow Fanglords, she abandoned the traditional tenets of the Cenarion Circle in favor of the vicious aspects of the viper. Channeling lightning, nature magic, and slumbering trances, she enforces Naralex's twisted slumber and works to spread the nightmare's corruption into the arid land above.

npc:lady-sarevess.text: Lady Sarevess. Lady Sarevess is a twisted naga sorceress dwelling within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, where she dabbles in dark sorceries. Within the Pool of Ask'ar, Lady Sarevess conducts her rituals in a flooded grotto of the ruined temple. A very twisted spellcaster, she dabbles in dark magic while the Twilight's Hammer cultists who also haunt the sunken temple pursue their own worship deeper in the cavern. Much like a sea witch of the deep oceans, Sarevess commands elemental currents and crackling arcs of lightning. Surrounded by loyal naga sentinels and summoned water elementals, she fiercely defends her sanctuary against any intruders who threaten her dark work.

npc:lord-cobrahn.text: Lord Cobrahn. Lord Cobrahn is one of the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang lurking deep within the Wailing Caverns. Once a night elf druid of Naralex's noble order, which hoped to heal the Barrens, he succumbed to the nightmare infecting the cavern springs. Taking a lethal serpent guise, Cobrahn now commands broods of deviate serpents and defends the twisted labyrinth. Before his fall, Cobrahn was one of the noble druids who followed Naralex. When Naralex ventured into the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens hoping to tap their underground springs and restore lush life to the arid wastes, Cobrahn accompanied him. However, when Naralex's Emerald Dream communion decayed into a twisting nightmare, Cobrahn's mind shattered alongside his brothers. Rather than channeling the traditional totemic beasts of Cenarion tradition, the nightmare warped Cobrahn's shapeshifting into something predatory and reptilian. He now commands a deadly serpentine form that he unleashes in battle. Flanked by venomous deviate pythons and bearing a vicious clawed right hand, he oversees his section of the grottos, violently purging anyone seeking to break the nightmare's hold on the caverns.

npc:lord-pythas.text: Lord Pythas. Lord Pythas, once a night elf warrior, is one of the four corrupted leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. Originally one of the personal guards of the druid Naralex, he fell victim to the nightmare tainting the oasis underground. Now he wields both martial might and twisted serpent magic against any who try to reach his slumbering master. Before his corruption, Pythas was a seasoned night elf warrior who served among the druid Naralex's personal guard when the expedition ventured into the dry wastes of the Barrens. Alongside his martial training, he took up the druidic arts in service of Naralex's dream of restoring lush life to the arid realm. However, physical discipline and martial valor offered no shelter against the insidious corruption waiting deep within the subterranean fissures. When Naralex's connection to the Emerald Dream was hijacked by dark nightmares, Pythas's mind succumbed alongside those of his fellow acolytes. Abandoning his former loyalty, he became one of the leaders of the Druids of the Fang. Where his fellow serpent lords favor cunning spellcasting or beast forms, Pythas seamlessly blends lethal combat prowess with nature magic. He now prowls the winding tunnels of the caverns, determined to defend the nightmare's twisted grip on the cavern spring.

npc:lord-serpentis.text: Lord Serpentis. Lord Serpentis is a corrupted night elf druid who stands as one of the four leaders of the rogue Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a druid of great power and prestige in the order of Naralex, he was twisted into madness when Naralex's dream became a nightmare within the subterranean springs. Now, he helps command the serpent-worshipping sect deep in the caverns where the corrupted Naralex lies slumbering. Before darkness overtook the cavern springs, Serpentis was a druid of great power and prestige, one of the noble order led by Naralex that hoped to use the caverns' springs and the Emerald Dream to heal the Barrens. However, when Naralex's vision became a corrupting nightmare, Serpentis was among the druids whose minds fell to the emerging madness. Succumbing completely to the corruption radiating from Naralex's twisted dreams, Serpentis and his fellow druids became the Druids of the Fang. Forsaking traditional Cenarion balance and the totem animals of old, they now seek to remake the Barrens to match their own twisted dreams rather than heal it. Serpentis rules the sect as one of its four leaders, alongside Lady Anacondra, Lord Cobrahn and Lord Pythas.

npc:lorgus-jett.text: Lorgus Jett. Lorgus Jett is a human member of the Twilight's Hammer cult operating within the flooded corridors of Blackfathom Deeps. Wandering the Moonshrine Ruins, he serves as a ruthless commander in the cult's service to the Old Gods. Horde leaders have singled him out as a primary target to disrupt the cult's encroaching presence along the Ashenvale coast. While many members of the Twilight's Hammer working under Blackfathom Deeps hail from orcish or tauren lineages, Lorgus Jett stands out as a human in the deep recesses of ancient night elf ruins. Roaming anywhere between the upper Moonshrine Ruins and the cavernous tunnels beyond the murloc defiler Gelihast, Jett coordinates the cult's dark rituals and violent ambitions.

npc:miner-johnson.text: Miner Johnson. Miner Johnson is an elusive, seasoned miner affiliated with the Defias Brotherhood deep inside the Deadmines. Tucked away in a side alcove alongside ordinary laborers, this dangerous prospector oversees excavation efforts ahead of the heavy machinery found deeper underground. Because he wanders the subterranean tunnels erratically, adventurers only occasionally cross his path. While hundreds of laborers pick at the subterranean veins of the Deadmines to supply Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress, Miner Johnson stands out as an unusually formidable figure among them. Lurking in a shadowed alcove to the left before the lumbering shredders of the Mast Room, he is far tougher and more aggressive than the regular workforce. His unpredictable presence makes him a legendary target for explorers traversing the Defias tunnels. The Defias Brotherhood's clandestine operation beneath Moonbrook requires vast amounts of raw ore to forge weapons, reinforce shafts, and assemble mechanical contraptions. Miners like Johnson provide the muscle behind the metal, hacking away at the rich mineral seams beneath Westfall. Anyone stumbling into Johnson's workspace will quickly discover that he defends his dig site with lethal fervor.

npc:mr-smite.text: Mr. Smite. Mr. Smite is the imposing tauren first mate serving aboard the Defias Brotherhood's flagship deep inside the Deadmines. An expert weaponmaster under Captain Greenskin, he commands the dockside approach to the hidden juggernaut with ruthless discipline. Intruders who face him must contend with his shifting arsenal and devastating physical strength. Guarding the docks of Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite serves as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. While the Defias Brotherhood is predominantly composed of disenfranchised humans and allied goblin tinkerers, Smite stands as a striking anomaly: a massive, battle-hardened tauren far from the plains of Kalimdor. Tasked with maintaining strict order among a rowdy pirate crew, he ensures that the labor fitting out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught proceeds without disruption. Smite is not merely a brute enforcer; he is a theatrical and versatile weaponmaster. He delights in toying with would-be heroes, deliberately prolonging combat to offer opponents a false sense of hope. When pressed, he unleashes a staggering, earth-shattering stomp that leaves foes stunned while he rummages through his nearby weapon chest. Beginning combat with a nimble dueling blade, he will escalate to twin cleaving reavers, and finally resort to his colossal two-handed warhammer when thoroughly provoked.

npc:mutanus-the-devourer.text: Mutanus the Devourer. Mutanus the Devourer is a monstrous, pale murloc manifested directly from the Emerald Nightmare. Lurking in the darkest recesses of the sleeping druid Naralex's mind, it emerges to devour anyone attempting to break the Nightmare's hold over the Wailing Caverns. Slaying this twisted aberration is the final step in freeing Naralex from his tormented slumber. When the night elf druid Naralex tapped into the underground springs beneath the Barrens, he aimed to restore life to the arid wastes by connecting them to the Emerald Dream. Instead, an ancient corruption known as the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's subconscious fears took physical form. The corruption gave that nightmare the shape of an immense, albino murloc.

npc:naralex.text: Naralex. Naralex is a night elf druid who sought to restore the parched Barrens to a lush forest using the powers of the Emerald Dream. Instead, his slumber was overtaken by a dark nightmare, twisting the Wailing Caverns beneath the earth and turning his followers into venomous fiends. Long before the Great Sundering, the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens were once a vibrant forest. Viewing this loss as a tragedy, Naralex journeyed to the Barrens with a cohort of devoted disciples to reverse the drought. Deep beneath the savannah, he discovered an intricate subterranean network of underground springs and rushing geysers, naming them the Wailing Caverns after the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed that by entering a deep trance and channeling the pristine energies of the Emerald Dream into these subterranean waters, the life-giving flow would reach the surface and cause the entire wasteland to bloom. Naralex seated himself in deep meditation deep within the subterranean caverns, but his noble design collapsed the moment his consciousness touched the realm of the Dream. Rather than finding peaceful fonts of wild nature, his mind was ensnared by a malignant, encroaching corruption—an Emerald Nightmare. The festering corruption seized the sleeping druid's body, transforming him into an open conduit through which dark energies bled into the living world. The pristine springs turned foul, sprouting mutated fungal blooms and warping the native beasts of the caverns into ravenous deviate horrors.

npc:oggleflint.text: Oggleflint. Beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint leads the trogg tribe in Ragefire Chasm. His pack climbs from lava-filled tunnels toward the surface, where he commands them near the cavern entrance and threatens the Horde capital above. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint and his troggs climbed from fiery tunnels into Ragefire Chasm. They carved a primitive domain among the molten rock and defend it with brutal force. Troggs have little advanced civilization, and Oggleflint rules his pack through sheer strength. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent diplomats into the chasm to make peace with the troggs. The troggs turned on them and killed them. Maur Grimtotem, one of the envoys, lies dead in the caverns under Oggleflint’s watch. Near the cavern entrance, the chieftain waits and strikes at outsiders who venture into the dark. Oggleflint’s tribe lives directly beneath Thrall’s capital, a hazard the Horde cannot tolerate. The troggs creep closer to the surface, and their volatile nature threatens to carry them into the Drag and Cleft of Shadow if left undisturbed.

npc:old-serra-kis.text: Old Serra'kis. Old Serra'kis is an ancient, massive threshadon dwelling in the submerged subterranean waters of Blackfathom Deeps. Hidden in a flooded cave beneath the ruins, the enormous beast is lethal to any who seek it out. The Twilight's Hammer has made its home in the sunken Moonshrine Ruins, but the dark waters beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum hide older, wilder things. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, lurks in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded cave beneath the ruins where few would think to look. Reaching Old Serra'kis requires plunging deep beneath the temple floor into a flooded cavern beneath the ruins. Lacking air pockets, the cave itself is as deadly as the beast within. Those who corner him find that Serra'kis possesses an unnatural shadow-leeching resilience, draining the life from his attackers while sustaining his own vitality in the murky darkness.

npc:overlord-ramtusk.text: Overlord Ramtusk. Overlord Ramtusk is a massive quilboar warlord who leads the warriors deep within Razorfen Kraul. Crying out for victory and for Agamaggan, he fights at the head of his elite guards, and striking him down shatters the martial backbone of the Kraul's defenders. Overlord Ramtusk holds command deep within the thorny maze of Razorfen Kraul, the quilboar stronghold in the southern Barrens. He goes into battle with a war cry to the boar demigod Agamaggan, and he rules the Kraul's fighters with unyielding authority. Within the winding brambles of the Kraul, Ramtusk directs the quilboar warriors. As their warlord, he maintains tight discipline among the bristled fighters defending the tribe's sanctum. Flanked by elite marksmen, Ramtusk fights like a frontline berserker, bellowing rallying shouts and unleashing earth-shattering slams that can break opposing battle lines in seconds.

npc:rhahk-zor.text: Rhahk'Zor. Rhahk'Zor is a hulking ogre serving as the head foreman within the Deadmines. Overseeing Edwin VanCleef's subterranean construction efforts, he keeps the Defias laborers and miners in line through sheer brute force and heavy-handed discipline. Deep beneath the rolling hills of Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood has transformed the abandoned gold mines of Moonbrook into an underground fortress. Coordinating this sprawling construction requires harsh discipline, a role filled by the ogre Rhahk'Zor. Appointed as head foreman, he oversees the excavation crews and laborers, driving them forward to carve out tunnels and assemble VanCleef's secret projects. Rhahk'Zor maintains order through relentless muscle rather than careful engineering. Armed with an immense stone-headed hammer, his idea of workplace supervision is direct and unforgiving. Defias diggers and goblin engineers alike step lively around him, knowing that falling behind schedule or showing defiance invites a crushing blow from the towering taskmaster.

npc:scarlet-commander-mograine.text: Scarlet Commander Mograine. Scarlet Commander Mograine serves as the military leader garrisoned inside the Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery. A zealous paladin of the Scarlet Crusade, he defends the chapel alongside High Inquisitor Whitemane. Both the Horde and Alliance target him to disrupt the zealots threatening Tirisfal Glades and the surrounding lands. Stationed within the grand Crusader's Chapel at the heart of the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Commander Mograine commands the standing garrison of the Scarlet Crusade. He wields the holy power of a paladin with ferocious dedication, relying on retribution, divine shields, and stunning blows to shatter any whom the Crusade deems corrupted or unclean.

npc:sneed.text: Sneed. Sneed is the Defias Brotherhood's goblin lumbermaster stationed deep within the Deadmines. Operating from the lumber chamber known as the Mast Room, he pilots a heavy shredder of his own design to process timber for Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut. While the Defias Brotherhood draws its core membership from disenfranchised human stonemasons and common laborers, building an ironclad warship requires specialist trades. Edwin VanCleef recruited Sneed specifically for his engineering know-how and ruthless goblin efficiency. Stationed in the Mast Room along the subterranean rail network, Sneed oversees the rapid felling, cutting, and shaping of timber needed to frame VanCleef's colossal dreadnaught. Sneed's primary concern is cutting costs and meeting deadlined quotas, consequences be damned. To speed up the process, he commands the floor from inside a customized shredder equipped with oversized buzz saws. The deadly machine turns raw trunks into shipbuilding timber in seconds. If cornered by intruders, Sneed relies on the armor of his machine to grind them down, but he is more than willing to scramble out of the wreckage and fight with his bare hands if his contraption fails.

npc:sneed-s-shredder.text: Sneed's Shredder. Sneed's Shredder is an imposing mechanised lumber harvester stationed deep within the Deadmines. Piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this deadly machine acts as both heavy industrial machinery for Edwin VanCleef's shipwrights and a terrifying perimeter defender. Within the goblin-dominated foundry of the Deadmines, mechanical shredders serve a dual purpose: processing vast amounts of timber and lumber required for Edwin VanCleef's hidden juggernaut, and serving as armored shock engines against intruders. Sneed, the overseer of the lumber works, operates this modified mechanical beast directly, turning an oversized buzzsaw into an instrument of defense. Defeating the machine does not end the threat. Sneed perches inside an open cockpit above the spinning blades, relying on heavy iron plating and terrifying clatter to scatter his foes. Even when the machinery breaks down and the shredder collapses in a shower of sparks, Sneed leaps from the smoking wreckage to fight to the bitter end.

npc:taragaman-the-hungerer.text: Taragaman the Hungerer. Beneath Orgrimmar, Taragaman the Hungerer prowls the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm. The Horde seeks to destroy the hulking felguard, feared as the demonic master behind the Searing Blade cult, and end the demonic taint beneath the city. Taragaman the Hungerer prowls among Ragefire Chasm's magma pools, threatening Orgrimmar below. Scouts and young warriors sent into the dark caverns see the demonic felguard as the Searing Blade cult's leader. With infernal strength, he bends the weak-willed and corrupts the passages beneath Thrall's fortress.

npc:targorr-the-dread.text: Targorr the Dread. Targorr the Dread is an infamous Blackrock orc executioner imprisoned deep within the Stormwind Stockade. Known for his brutal tortures of captured Stormwind soldiers, his execution was indefinitely delayed by bureaucratic incompetence and corruption. When the Stockade erupted into revolt under the Defias Brotherhood, Targorr broke free and allied with the rioting convicts. Before his capture, Targorr the Dread served as the supreme executioner for the Blackrock clan under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg. Operating out of the occupied ruins in Redridge, his cruelty stood out as exceptionally savage even by the violent standards of the Dark Horde. Stormwind guards and militiamen who fought to defend the borderlands were subjected to agonizing torment and slow death at his hands, making his name one of the most reviled in the kingdom. When Alliance forces finally managed to capture Targorr alive, he was brought in chains to the capital and locked inside the high-security Stockade to await execution. However, the rot within Stormwind's judicial and political bureaucracy stalled the proceedings. Paralyzed by graft, endless paperwork, and neglect, the courts failed to deliver the death sentence he had earned, leaving a bloodthirsty war criminal sitting in a cell beneath the heart of the city. When the Defias Brotherhood staged their violent prison break, Targorr saw his opportunity. Breaking free from his cell, the ruthless orc threw his lot in with the Defias rioters, turning his cellblock into a slaughterhouse. With the prison entirely out of Warden Thelwater's control, towns like Lakeshire—still nursing the bitter wounds Targorr inflicted on their defenders—seek adventurers willing to venture into the riots and bring back the butcher's head.

npc:twilight-lord-kelris.text: Twilight Lord Kelris. Twilight Lord Kelris is an orc warlock and high-ranking leader within the Twilight's Hammer cult operating deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. From his perch in the Moonshrine Sanctum, he leads dark rituals in worship of the primordial hydra Aku'mai, aiming to usher in a reign of cosmic chaos. Twilight Lord Kelris directs the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who seized the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. For years, Kelris slipped through the grasp of watchful eyes in Darnassus, evading the Argent Dawn and earning a grim reputation: whenever ancient malice stirred across Kalimdor, Kelris was suspected of orchestrating it. Rather than serving warlords or clans, this orc has pledged himself entirely to the Old Gods, seeking to unmake mortal civilization and return Azeroth to a state of absolute, primordial chaos. Within the Moonshrine Sanctum, Kelris oversees the cult's worship of Aku'mai, a vicious three-headed hydra and servant of an Old God. Allied with the naga, the Twilight's Hammer occupies the drowned temple, and Kelris presides over the cult's rites, sacrificing innocents to Aku'mai for power.

npc:verdan-the-everliving.text: Verdan the Everliving. Verdan the Everliving is a colossal bog beast lurking deep within the verdant tunnels of the Wailing Caverns. He dwells amid the nightmare spreading from the sleeping druid Naralex, alongside the corrupted Druids of the Fang, and violently attacks any who venture into his damp hollows. Verdan is a hulking bog beast, an elemental of foliage, silt, and mire that lurks in the overgrown depths of the Wailing Caverns. Nothing is known of him from before the caverns fell to corruption; he is simply the largest and most dangerous creature in their lush, flooded hollows.

npc:viscous-fallout.text: Viscous Fallout. Viscous Fallout is a toxic water elemental wandering the irradiated corridors of Gnomeregan, a living mass of the poison that fouled the city after Mekgineer Thermaplugg's devastating radiation release. When Gnomeregan was flooded with radiation on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's treacherous advice to wipe out the invading troggs, the fallout left the city's lower levels awash in toxic slime and contamination. Viscous Fallout is a water elemental of that poisoned depth, its very substance thick with the city's toxic waste. Where it came from before the fall is not known. Now, the creature is little more than a living pool of toxic sludge, drifting through the irradiated lower passages. Spewing volleys of toxin, Viscous Fallout lashes out at anything in its path. Striking it down is a grim necessity for those venturing into Gnomeregan to cleanse the tainted depths.

subzone:camp-narache.text: Camp Narache. Camp Narache is a secluded village nestled upon Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It serves as the ancestral home of the Hawkwind tribe and the proving ground where young tauren begin their training. Sheltered high above the plains, the camp maintains ancient traditions while constantly guarding against encroaching quilboar and lingering centaur threats. Situated at the northern edge of the elevated Red Cloud Mesa, Camp Narache is the primary settlement of the Hawkwind tribe. The village consists of several large hide lodges and pavilions, including a communal tent for wounded braves, an armory, a bakery tent, and a spirit lounge dedicated to meditation and ancestral communion. At the center of the camp, tribal elders and path trainers stand in a circle at the heart of the camp, where the venerable Greatmother Hawkwind still offers guidance, guiding newly initiated youth as they step into their roles as defenders of the Earth Mother. Though naturally fortified by the steep sheer cliffs of the mesa, Camp Narache faces persistent unrest. Bristleback quilboar from Brambleblade Ravine continuously encroach upon Hawkwind lands, while centaur scouts linger in the distance. Young hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors prove their mettle here by culling the aggressive local wildlife, protecting the village's water well, and turning back quilboar raiders before descending the grand path into the wider valleys of Mulgore.

subzone:coldridge-valley.text: Coldridge Valley. Coldridge Valley is a sheltered, snow-covered vale tucked into the southwestern heights of Dun Morogh. Centered around the hamlet of Anvilmar, it serves as the training ground where young dwarves and gnome refugees first take up arms in service of Ironforge. A single tunnel, Coldridge Pass, connects this secluded hollow to the wider mountain realm. Cradled by sheer mountain cliffs, Coldridge Valley remains largely cut off from the bustling trade routes of Dun Morogh. At its heart sits Anvilmar, a sturdy stone hall and hamlet where veteran dwarven instructors and displaced gnome scholars train fresh recruits in the arts of battle, stealth, and sorcery. Outside the warmth of Anvilmar's hearths, the valley floor is carpeted in thick snow and prowled by boars and hungry winter wolves, providing novices with their first real taste of frontier survival. Despite its isolation, Coldridge Valley faces immediate danger from two relentless enemies. Indigenous Frostmane trolls have established camps like the Frostmane Hovel, skirmishing with mountaineers and defending their ancestral claims against dwarven encroachment. Worse still, savage Rockjaw troggs have overrun Coldridge Pass, the natural tunnel linking the valley to Kharanos. Until these subterranean brutes are pushed back, travelers and supplies cannot freely move between the valley and the high seat of Ironforge.

subzone:deathknell.text: Deathknell. Deathknell is a fortified village nestled in a secluded valley in southwestern Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the primary awakening grounds for newly freed undead breaking free from the Lich King's grasp to join the Forsaken. Besieged by mindless Scourge remnants, local zealots, and aggressive wildlife, the settlement is a harsh proving ground for those claiming a place in Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. Tucked away behind jagged hills just north of the Silverpine border, Deathknell is where newly awakened undead first open their eyes to their bleak reality. Unlike most settlements in Tirisfal Glades that preserved their human names from the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, Deathknell was explicitly renamed by the undead who claimed it. The town itself is cleaved in two: the Forsaken cling stubbornly to the southern grounds around the old church, while the northern half—including the village forge—remains overrun by mindless Scourge zombies and feral ghouls. Elite Deathguards keep the narrow gorge out of the valley securely sealed against intruders, allowing local caretakers to induct new arrivals into the Banshee Queen's service. Survival in Deathknell is precarious. To the northwest, Night Web's Hollow—a gold mine vital for the Forsaken's fledgling economy—has been lost to monstrous spiders. To the southeast, an aggressive encampment of the Scarlet Crusade maintains constant watch, trading couriers with their strongholds to the east and probing the valley's defenses. Meanwhile, the village caretakers must continually fight off the mindless undead wandering the northern ruins while gathering scrap metal, tools, and supplies to equip newly arisen souls for the long road ahead.

subzone:northshire-abbey.text: Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey trains new defenders in Northshire Valley, among Elwynn Forest's northern foothills. Rebuilt after the First War, it is the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire and a leading school for those answering Stormwind's call. Clerics from Lordaeron came south centuries ago to spread the Holy Light and founded the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics and their abbey. The monastery soon became part of kingdom life, caring for the sick and tending to the young Guardian Medivh during his years in a coma. In the First War, brigands and the Orcish Horde attacked it repeatedly, and the abbey was destroyed. After the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the region in the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild the sanctuary and refounded its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire. Northshire Abbey trains volunteers, militia recruits, and novices who hope to defend Stormwind. Its Main Hall, Hall of Arms, and Library Wing house instructors in martial, arcane, and holy arts, while scouts and rogues train in the outer yards. The Knights of the Silver Hand keep watch, but peace remains fragile. Kobolds overrun nearby mines, aggressive wolves prowl the orchards, and Defias Brotherhood agents stalk the valley roads. They steal ancient scrolls and sacred librams from the abbey's archives.

subzone:sen-jin-village.text: Sen'jin Village. Sen'jin Village shelters the Darkspear on Durotar's southern shore. Vol'jin founded it after Zalazane drove his people from the Echo Isles, naming it for his fallen father. The villagers endure exile and prepare to reclaim their home. Sen'jin Village shelters the Darkspear survivors on Durotar's shore. After the witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized the Echo Isles, Chieftain Vol'jin led them across the strait to the mainland. They raised crude huts beneath coastal cliffs, facing the water and the home they had lost. The village bears the name of Sen'jin, Vol'jin's father, who was captured and sacrificed by murlocs during the Third War. Though the Darkspear are closely allied with Thrall's Horde, exile remains their burden. Each day, the lost isles lie just across the shallows. Life in Sen'jin Village turns on preparation and defense. Quilboar raids, aggressive sea beasts, and Zalazane's hexes from across the sea threaten the villagers. Herbal remedies and potent alchemical spirits help sustain them. Vol'jin coordinates the tribe's wider defense from the Horde capital, while local shamans, hunters, and scouts gather recruits arriving from the Valley of Trials. They seek resources, guard Durotar's southern flank, and plan Zalazane's downfall.

subzone:shadowglen.text: Shadowglen. Young night elves begin their training in Shadowglen, beneath the boughs of Teldrassil. The vale gathers around Aldrassil, where elders, priestesses, and mentors guide them before they travel farther into the world. Shadowglen lies beneath the northeastern boughs of Teldrassil, ringed by high ridges that shelter it from the rest of the world. Eternal dusk falls over the vale, where Aldrassil rises as a massive barrow-tree. Its hollowed trunk houses elders, priestesses, and mentors who guide young night elves beginning their training. A narrow mountain pass leads south toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar. This single route out leaves the sanctuary sheltered and peaceful. Danger reaches even this sheltered vale. Shadowthread Cave lies in the extreme northwest, where venomous spiders threaten the glade. Young defenders drive back the encroaching vermin and untamed wildlife before venturing farther among Teldrassil's boughs.

subzone:valley-of-trials.text: Valley of Trials. In the Valley of Trials, young Horde recruits test their strength in southern Durotar. Orcs and Darkspear trolls face the valley’s wildlife and dangers before they leave ready to defend their people. Young fighters face the Valley of Trials before they venture into Durotar. Chieftains and trainers watch over them from The Den, a shelter carved into the cliffs. In the sunlit gulch, recruits hunt scorpids, cull aggressive boars, and keep lazy peons in line as they harvest scarce timber. The trial is hard, and only those who prove their mettle earn the right to leave as soldiers of the Horde. Those who fail are left beneath the desert sun.

topic:alliance-of-lordaeron.text: Alliance of Lordaeron. The Alliance of Lordaeron was the historic grand coalition of the seven human kingdoms, Khaz Modan dwarves, Wildhammer gryphon riders, gnomes, and high elves formed to resist the Old Horde in the Second War. Led militarily by Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and diplomatically by King Terenas Menethil II, it shattered the invading orcish forces and secured the Eastern Kingdoms. Though political fractures and the devastation of the Scourge tore it apart during the Third War, its legacy laid the foundation for the current Alliance. Following the horrific sack of Stormwind in the First War, Regent Lord Anduin Lothar brought the battered southern refugees across the Great Sea to Capital City. Pleading their cause before King Terenas Menethil II, Lothar convinced him to gather the rulers of the human nations in council. Old rivalries and border tensions ran deep, but the threat of the Horde outweighed them. Choosing Lothar as their Supreme Commander, the seven human nations bound themselves together in a desperate pact. Facing brutal orcish warriors, dark warlocks, and monstrous red dragons, the Alliance forged entirely new doctrines of war. Archbishop Alonsus Faol and Lothar established the Knights of the Silver Hand, elevating holy paladins like Uther the Lightbringer to counter the Horde's dark magic. When the war raged across the Hinterlands and quelled the siege of Aerie Peak, Kurdran Wildhammer pledged his fierce gryphon riders to rule the skies. Shortly thereafter, the Bronzebeard dwarves and Gnomeregan gnomes were liberated, joining high elven rangers under Alleria Windrunner. Despite the treacherous betrayal of King Perenolde of Alterac, the grand coalition drove the Horde back to Blackrock Spire and crushed their dominion. Victory brought bitterness rather than enduring peace. Bitter disputes erupted over the high taxes required to maintain the orc internment camps and rebuild the blasted kingdom of Stormwind. Seeing little personal gain, Gilneas built the Greymane Wall and severed ties, Stromgarde departed over territorial and prisoner quarrels, and Quel'Thalas pulled back behind its enchanted runestones. The coalition that remained under King Terenas attempted to weather the political storm, only to be utterly dismantled during the Third War when the Cult of the Damned and the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron. Arthas Menethil's betrayal tore the heart out of the kingdom, ending the golden age of the northern realm.

topic:alterac-kingdom.text: Alterac (kingdom). Alterac was one of the seven historic human kingdoms, nestled high in the rugged Alterac Mountains. During the Second War, its ruler, King Aiden Perenolde, made a treacherous pact with the Old Horde to spare his realm, leading to the kingdom's military downfall and total collapse. Today, its ruined capital lies abandoned in the snow, while dispossessed nobles and outlaws wage a guerrilla war under the banner of the Syndicate. Alterac arose thousands of years ago as an Arathorian city-state following the Troll Wars. Settlers capitalized on strategic mountain passes and trading outposts, eventually establishing an independent realm when the empire fractured. Though rugged and mountainous, Alterac bordered the prosperous lands of Lordaeron and Stromgarde. Historically, it fielded tough mountain fighters, but enduring border friction with Thoras Trollbane's Stromgarde left the kingdom politically isolated from its neighbors long before the Dark Portal ever opened. When Sir Anduin Lothar forged the Alliance of Lordaeron, King Aiden Perenolde joined only with deep reluctance. As Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde swept north, Perenolde concluded humanity was doomed and secretly struck a deal with the Warchief. In exchange for the safety of Alterac, Perenolde opened fortified mountain passes, conspired against Alliance forces, and even dispatched soldiers and sailors to assist the Horde's siege of Lordaeron. The treachery allowed the orcs to reach Capital City far ahead of schedule, shaking the Alliance to its core when the truth was laid bare. Retribution was swift. Stromgarde's forces marched into the mountains, exposing Perenolde's treason and breaking Alterac's military. King Terenas Menethil II placed the fallen nation under martial law, while arguments over who should inherit the throne paralyzed Alliance diplomats for years. Following the kingdom's collapse, King Perenolde died in disgrace. His son, Lord Aliden Perenolde, rallied the bitter, displaced nobility to form the Syndicate. Wearing the orange cloth of their fallen homeland, these bandits and mercenaries now fight ruthlessly to reclaim their ancestral holdings across Hillsbrad and Alterac.

topic:anduin-lothar.text: Anduin Lothar. Sir Anduin Lothar, known as the Lion of Stormwind, was the last descendant of the ancient Arathi bloodline and the Supreme Commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron. A childhood companion of King Llane Wrynn and the Guardian Medivh, Lothar led humanity through the horrors of the First War and rallied the northern nations during the Second War before falling at Blackrock Mountain. Carrying the ancient bloodline of the Arathi kings, Lothar grew up within Stormwind's royal court alongside Prince Llane Wrynn and Medivh. The trio embarked on reckless excursions into the wilderness, skirmishing with Gurubashi trolls in Stranglethorn Vale. Lothar rose rapidly through Stormwind's martial ranks, joining the King's Honor Guard and earning renown as an Armsman of the Brotherhood of the Horse. Arriving on the shores of Lordaeron, Lothar presented the grim reality of the Horde to King Terenas Menethil II. Invoking his ancestral Arathi lineage and diplomatic gravitas, he unified the human realms, Ironforge dwarves, and high elves into the Grand Alliance of Lordaeron. Named Supreme Commander of the united forces, Lothar spearheaded the campaign that pushed the Horde back south to the foot of Blackrock Mountain. There, in a fateful clash near the end of the Second War, Lothar was slain by Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. His death did not shatter the Alliance; instead, it galvanized his lieutenant, Turalyon, to lead the charge that broke the Horde forever.

topic:argent-dawn.text: Argent Dawn. The Argent Dawn is a neutral, knightly order dedicated to stamping out malevolent threats across Azeroth, most notably the Scourge and the Burning Legion. Formed by survivors of the Knights of the Silver Hand who rejected the fanatical zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade, they welcome champions of any race or faction who honor the cause of the Light. From their fortified sanctuary at Light's Hope Chapel to far-flung outposts across Kalimdor, they stand on the front lines against darkness. When Highlord Alexandros Mograine fell and Lordaeron collapsed into ruin, the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand broke into bitter disagreement. Many survivors surrendered to grief and paranoia, morphing into the xenophobic Scarlet Crusade. Yet veterans like Lord Maxwell Tyrosus recognized that their former comrades had abandoned the true tenets of the Holy Light. Refusing to succumb to madness or abandon the dead kingdom, they split away to form the Argent Dawn—an order committed to defending Azeroth alongside anyone willing to fight, whether Alliance or Horde. The Dawn's primary stronghold is Light's Hope Chapel, situated in the blighted expanse of the Eastern Plaguelands. From this consecrated bastion, the order coordinates an unending war against Kel'Thuzad's necromancers and skeletal legions. Operating forward camps at Chillwind Camp and outside the Bulwark in Tirisfal Glades, Argent officers issue enchanted commissions to adventurers, paying bounties in exchange for Scourgestones wrested from fallen undead. Despite lacking the raw manpower of the Scarlet Crusade, the Dawn holds the line through perseverance, unity, and unshakable discipline. While Lordaeron remains their principal battleground, the Argent Dawn maintains an active watch across Kalimdor and the capitals of the world. They keep diplomatic presences in Stormwind City, Darnassus, and the goblin trade town of Everlook. Farther afield, operatives like Delgren the Purifier contest demonic cults in Darkshore and Ashenvale, while scouts in Desolace and the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps investigate sinister threats involving the Shadow Council and the Twilight's Hammer cult.

topic:arthas-menethil.text: Arthas Menethil. Once the golden prince of Lordaeron and a celebrated paladin of the Silver Hand, Arthas Menethil fell from grace during the Third War while pursuing the demonic orchestrators of the plague. After claiming the cursed runeblade Frostmourne in the frozen north, he surrendered his soul, murdered his father King Terenas, and spearheaded the destruction of his own homeland as the Scourge's dark champion. Born to King Terenas Menethil II, Arthas was raised to embody the ideals of the Alliance of Lordaeron. Trained in combat by Muradin Bronzebeard and inducted into the Order of the Silver Hand under the tutelage of Uther the Lightbringer, he was revered by high and low alike as the future of humanity. Bold, skilled, and fiercely protective of his people, he fought tenaciously against Blackrock clan orc incursions and forest troll warbands. Yet beneath his radiant exterior lay an uncompromising pride and an obsessive dread of failure.

topic:black-dragonflight.text: Black dragonflight. Once the stalwart Earth-Warders charged by the titans to safeguard Azeroth's deep subterranean realms, the black dragonflight fell to madness and treachery. Corrupted by the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods, their leader Neltharion became Deathwing, turning his brood into one of the most destructive and hated forces on the planet. Today, their surviving scions weave plots from the shadows and wage covert wars against mortal kingdoms. Long ago, the Titan Khaz'goroth bestowed his blessing upon Neltharion, creating the black dragonflight to watch over the earth, raise mountains, and guard Azeroth's deep caverns. For ages, they stood alongside the other flights as patient, unyielding guardians. Yet their intimate bond with the world's subterranean foundations proved their undoing. Dwelling within the deepest hollows, they lay dangerously close to the sunken prisons of the Old Gods. Over centuries, dark whispers eroded the noble Earth-Warder's mind, driving him to madness and twisting his entire brood into vicious instruments of ruin. During the ancient War of the Ancients, Neltharion shattered the unity of dragonkind, turning upon his kin as Deathwing the Destroyer. Ever since, the black flight has waged relentless, spiteful war against the red, blue, green, and bronze flights, who view their cruelty as an absolute profanation of life. Rather than tending the soil, black dragons now wield molten magma, black magic, and searing brimstone to scorch the lands they once nurtured, finding delight in sowing discord, misery, and endless strife across mortal realms.

topic:blackrock-clan.text: Blackrock clan. The Blackrock clan is a martial orcish clan renowned for its strict military discipline, unmatched blacksmithing, and central role in the First and Second Wars. Today, the clan is deeply fractured: while some veterans follow Thrall in the New Horde, a vicious and renegade splinter group known as the Dark Horde occupies the upper peaks of Blackrock Mountain under Rend Blackhand. Hailing from Draenor, the Blackrock clan made its name through rigid hierarchy, heavy armor, and mastery over the forge. Under Chieftain Blackhand, they served as the brutal core of the Old Horde during the invasion of Azeroth, laying siege to Stormwind. When Orgrim Doomhammer slew Blackhand to cleanse the Horde of Gul'dan's direct puppet mastery, leadership of both the clan and the Horde remained firmly in Blackrock hands through the grueling campaigns of the Second War. Following the Horde's catastrophic defeat at Blackrock Mountain, the clan shattered. Many warriors were rounded up and placed in Alliance internment camps, later to be liberated by Thrall and inducted into his reformed New Horde. However, unrepentant elements rallied behind Blackhand's sons, Rend and Maim. This faction retreated into the heights of Blackrock Spire, forming the hostile Dark Horde alongside remnants of the Dragonmaw and other rogue clans. Today, Rend Blackhand claims the mantle of true Warchief from his throne in Blackrock Spire. The Dark Horde maintains an uneasy and treacherous truce with the Dark Iron dwarves who lurk in the molten depths below, all while waging war against both the Alliance and Thrall's Horde. Uncompromising, demon-tainted remnants of the clan have also been spotted lingering in Lordaeron, seeking to revive dark sacrificial rituals.

topic:bronzebeard-clan.text: Bronzebeard clan. The Bronzebeard clan is the ruling dwarven royal line and dominant population of Ironforge. Following their victory in the ancient War of the Three Hammers, they forged strong ties with humanity and the gnomes, standing today under King Magni Bronzebeard as a cornerstone of the Alliance. Long ago, dwarven society in Ironforge flourished under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died of old age roughly 230 years ago, simmering rivalries erupted into civil war. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded the traditional garrison and largest standing army within Ironforge, successfully driving both the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from under the mountain. When Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan mounted an assault to reconquer Khaz Modan, Madoran Bronzebeard led his clan in a decisive campaign that shattered the Dark Iron host, solidifying Bronzebeard supremacy over Ironforge. Human kingdoms first encountered the Bronzebeards nearly two millennia ago, building mutual respect through shared mastery of metalcraft, trade, and a passion for battle. When the Orcish Horde swept through the continent in the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard brought his realm into the Alliance of Lordaeron. Despite withstanding brutal sieges within their subterranean fortress, Bronzebeard engineers, gunners, and demolitionists provided pivotal firepower and arms that helped turn the tide of the war.

topic:burning-blade-clan.text: Burning Blade clan. Once an ancient orcish clan renowned for its deadly blademasters and consumed by chaotic frenzy during the early wars, the Burning Blade now largely persists as a sinister demon-worshiping cult. Its acolytes infiltrate Durotar and the Barrens under the direction of the Shadow Council. Meanwhile, a handful of honorable blademasters have forsaken its demonic corruption to serve Warchief Thrall in the New Horde. Originating in the lands of Draenor alongside clans like the Warsong, the Burning Blade were long respected for the lethal tradition of their blademasters. When they drank the blood of Mannoroth and marched through the Dark Portal into Azeroth during the First War, however, the clan fractured mentally. By the Second War, they were scarcely an organized society, behaving instead like a berserk force of nature. Nomadic and demented, they threw themselves into battle with total disregard for survival, requiring ogres to hold them in check until unleashed. Ultimately, their numbers were battered and routed near the Dark Portal by the Alliance. Following the Second War, the surviving remnants of the Burning Blade split dramatically. A disciplined contingent of blademasters swore solemn oaths to liberate their people from demonic enslavement, pledging their blades directly to Warchief Thrall as his personal honor guard. Yet a far larger portion of the scattered clan fell entirely under the sway of the Burning Legion and the Shadow Council, morphing into a clandestine cult of warlocks, fel acolytes, and conspirators lurking throughout Kalimdor. The modern cult operates covens across Kalimdor, troubling newly arrived orcs and Darkspear trolls from their first days in the Valley of Trials. Burning Blade warlocks inhabit Thunder Ridge, and garrison a major hideout within Skull Rock near Orgrimmar's eastern gates. Their cultists rally around dark relics like the Demon Seed and harvest souls for demonic rituals, making them a primary internal menace against the fledgling Horde's stability in Durotar and the Barrens.

topic:burning-legion.text: Burning Legion. The Burning Legion is an infinite, apocalyptic host of demons led by the fallen titan Sargeras, dedicated to scouring all life from creation. Having already shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the demons remain Azeroth's most relentless nemesis, orchestrating the corruption of the orcs and the horrors of the Third War. Long ago, Sargeras stood as the champion of the titans, tasked with hunting down and imprisoning the demons that plagued the cosmos. Over countless ages of battling their evil, he grew disillusioned and concluded that creation itself was fatally flawed and must be unmade in flame. To enact his crusade, he freed the demons he had imprisoned, bending them to his will through fel magic. He augmented their chaos with the intellect of the corrupted eredar—elevating Archimonde and Kil'jaeden as his chief lieutenants—and forged an unstoppable engine of cosmic annihilation. Ten millennia ago, the reckless sorceries of the Highborne drew the Legion's gaze to Azeroth. Whispering through the Well of Eternity, Sargeras seduced Queen Azshara and her councilor Xavius with promises of reshaping the world into paradise. Instead, the portal unleashed commanders like Mannoroth and Archimonde alongside swarms of doomguard, felhounds, and flaming infernals. The ensuing war reduced Kalimdor's civilization to ruin before an alliance of night elves, dragonflights, and demigods collapsed the gateway. The catastrophic implosion tore the supercontinent apart in the Great Sundering, casting the ruined lands across vast new seas.
